title: Arkis approves DEX protocols by implementation, treating Uniswap v4 hooks as code requiring individual review
content:
A.6.1.1.1.3.7.2.2.5 sets two joint conditions for a DEX position to count in margin calculations: "(1) all assets to which a pool has exposure are approved as marginable assets, and (2) the protocol is either Curve-ng stableswap, Uniswap v2, Uniswap v3, **Uniswap v4 vanilla (no hooks)**, or Uniswap v4 using **hook(s) that have been onboarded via direct integration within the Spark Liquidity Layer**." Failing either in full, "the pool is treated as an unapproved asset/product" — the 100% haircut bucket.

The second condition is the substantive one. Approving an *asset* is a judgment about an issuer and a market; approving a *pool* requires a judgment about the code that governs it. Uniswap v4's hooks are arbitrary contracts invoked on swap, mint and burn, which means two v4 pools holding identical approved assets can behave completely differently — one a plain AMM, the other able to alter pricing, block withdrawals, or extract value on exit.

So asset-level approval is insufficient by construction, and the rule says so by enumerating protocol versions rather than protocol names. "Uniswap" is not approved; four specific implementations are.

The hook exception is the interesting part of the design. Rather than banning hooks outright, it reuses an approval Spark already performs elsewhere: a hook counts if it has been "onboarded via direct integration within the Spark Liquidity Layer" — meaning Spark's own capital is already exposed to that code under its own review process. One diligence effort serves both purposes, and the margin engine inherits a decision made with real money at stake rather than a separate, cheaper sign-off.

The conservatism has a cost: the fastest-innovating part of the AMM landscape is excluded from margin credit by default, and gaining credit requires an integration commitment, not just an assessment.
description: Only Curve-ng stableswap and Uniswap v2, v3 and vanilla v4 qualify; v4 pools with hooks are accepted solely if those hooks were onboarded via direct Spark Liquidity Layer integration.
